GK-08.c01: Space around your vehicle is **time**: when something goes wrong, space gives you time to think and act.
A truck needs more space than a car because it **takes up more room** and needs more room to stop and turn.
Manage space on every side (ahead, behind, sides, above, below) plus space for turns and crossing traffic.
GK-08.c02: The space **ahead** is the most important space, because a smaller vehicle ahead can usually stop faster than your truck.
Below 40 mph, keep at least **1 second for every 10 feet** of vehicle length; above 40 mph, **add 1 second** (once, not per extra 10 mph).
Example: a 40-ft truck needs **4 seconds** (5 above 40 mph); a 60-ft rig needs 6 seconds (7 above 40 mph).
Measure by counting "one thousand-and-one…" from when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed landmark until you reach it; slippery roads need **more** space.
GK-08.c03: Trucks get tailgated when **traveling slowly** (often uphill) or in **bad weather**; with a heavy load, stay in the right lane where possible.
If tailgated, **avoid quick changes**: signal early and slow down very gradually, because a sudden slowdown is how the tailgater hits you.
**Increase your following distance** ahead, so you won't need to brake or swerve suddenly and the tailgater can pass more easily.
**Do not speed up**, since being tailgated at a low speed is safer, and avoid tricks like turning on taillights or blinking brake lights.
GK-08.c04: Stay **centered in your lane** to keep some clearance on both sides.
Avoid traveling next to other vehicles: a driver may **swerve into your lane**, or you may be boxed in when you need to change lanes.
**Strong winds** can push you out of your lane, especially lighter vehicles and when coming out of a tunnel.
GK-08.c05: **Do not trust posted heights** at bridges and overpasses, because repaving or packed snow may have lowered the clearance.
An **empty** van sits higher than a loaded one, so a bridge you cleared loaded may not clear empty.
Not sure you will fit → **take another route**; where the road tilts, move a little toward the center.
Before backing, get out and check for overhanging objects such as **tree branches or electric wires**.
GK-08.c06: Space **under** the vehicle can be very small when it is heavily loaded.
Watch for **dirt roads and unpaved yards**, and cross drainage channels carefully so the vehicle's ends don't drag.
Don't risk getting hung up on **railroad tracks**, especially with low-clearance trailers.
GK-08.c07: Right turns: turn slowly and **turn wide as you complete the turn** (button hook), keeping the back near the curb so no one passes on the right.
**Do not swing left** before a right turn (jug handle); a driver behind may pull up on your right and get hit.
If the turn puts you in the oncoming lane, leave room or stop and wait, but **do not back up**.
Left turns: start only at the **center of the intersection**; with 2 left-turn lanes, use the **right-hand** (outside) lane.
GK-08.c08: Trucks accelerate slowly and take up a lot of room, so joining traffic needs a **much larger gap** than a car.
Acceleration depends on the load; when heavily loaded, allow **even more room**.
Start across a road only when sure you can get **all the way across** before any traffic reaches you.
